en.html:
As armored warriors went, she was an unusual sight.

No sword. No other blade, spear, staff—nothing of that kind.
Long claws instead. Three sharp points projected from the back of each hand, catching the twilight and shining orange.

Tiger claws.

Right up close, probably more effective than a sword. A design specialized for hand-to-hand combat, then?

The standard answer was simple. Do not enter her reach. Settle it at the reach of a long sword. Use the extra distance, attack without letting her attack back, and win.

Excellent plan.
Only one small requirement: the long sword.

I felt at our waist with my left hand. Where it should have been, nothing. A wakizashi was all we had.

This I had expected. I was not disappointed; I was merely considering how thoroughly reality had refused to help. A wakizashi's blade was short. Use it, and I must come close. Into her preferred fighting ground, personally.

Either of our previous weapons would have spared us this—the huge nodachi that had been Muramasa's main weapon, or its replacement, the sword a little over three shaku long. But wishing would not bring either back.

The Silver Star had taken both. The first, smashed into material for its eggs. The second, swallowed and lost in a vortex of gravity.

This wakizashi. Nothing else was left.

en.html:
I watched Chachamaru's three claws. Their number was not the problem.

In performance and in skill, she was almost certainly equipped for close combat. On our side, the opposite. I was less used to handling a wakizashi than a long sword, and our armor was not built around small weapons either.

Muramasa was orthodox. Heavy swords, in the air or on the ground—that was the work her performance was designed for. At touching distance, that performance could not come out properly.

And this was not the end of our disadvantages. More were available.

Chachamaru could hardly have missed what weapon we carried. Even so, she stood watching. Clearly not out of caution. She had no need to attack. Keep me here, and her purpose was served.

Turn that reasoning around, and there was my condition for victory. I did not necessarily have to defeat her. I did have to break through, as quickly as possible, and reach the keep.

If time simply passed, she would win and I would lose without our weapons even meeting.
The Forged Bomb would settle it.

So. Tactically at a disadvantage, and strategically forbidden to wait. Knowing this was the work I did badly, I still had to go straight in and do it.

Half-defeated before starting. That was not excessive pessimism; that was the position.

Muramasa released the left-arm armor.
The next instant, with a dull sound, my left shoulder came out of its socket.

...Nothing mysterious about it. The enemy's powerful arms were forcing that joint inward. Remove its steel support suddenly, leave only weak human flesh, and of course it would give way.

An electric shock of pain ran through me.
Nearly blew every thought clean out.
